description: Static security scanner for ML model files — detects pickle bombs, Keras Lambda RCE and GGUF template injection, and generates CycloneDX / SPDX AI-BOMs (AIBOM) as EU AI Act, CRA and FDA §524B evidence.

written.description: Produces the compliance artefact as well as the verdict: a CycloneDX or SPDX bill of materials for a model file, alongside the Keras, GGUF and ONNX payloads it found while reading it.

alive.last_commit_message:
feat(comply): add aisbom comply documentation packs (#133)

* feat(comply): add aisbom comply documentation packs

`aisbom comply <target> --framework {eu-ai-act|fda}` scans a target and
writes a folder of regulator-facing documents pre-filled from the scan.

- eu-ai-act: an Annex XI technical-documentation skeleton, an Article
  53(1)(d) training-content summary in the sections of the Commission's
  template (24 July 2025), the SBOM, and an index.
- fda: the SBOM, OpenVEX and CycloneDX VEX (with OSV CVE statements for
  exact pins), a component support table, and an index.

A field is filled only from something the scan read, and names its
source. Everything else is left as "TODO (provider)" rather than
guessed. A test bans verdict language in every generated file, each
document carries a template version and a not-legal-advice disclaimer,
and a scan with an unreadable target writes no pack and exits 1.

score and comply now share one scan-and-refuse-partial helper. The
README Privacy section discloses the cli_score and cli_comply events
and the lookups comply triggers. docs/comply.md lists every field and
where its value comes from.

* fix(comply): list Keras, GGUF and ONNX threats in the findings summary

Appendix A only read pickle properties, so a CRITICAL Keras, GGUF or ONNX file was summarised as 'none' beside the threats the bundled SBOM records. Every per-format threat property is now listed, and a HIGH or CRITICAL file with no recognised property points at the risk rating and sbom.json instead of reading 'none'.
